Let $x$ be a motion and put $u(t):=\omega_{0}x(t)+ix'(t)$, so that $\zeta=e^{i\omega_{0}t}u/\sqrt{2\omega_{0}}$ and $\operatorname{Im}u=\sqrt{2\omega_{0}}\bigl(\cos(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Im}\zeta-\sin(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Re}\zeta\bigr)$ by [F2]. From $x''=-\omega_{0}^{2}x-(\varepsilon\gamma/m)x'$ of the model, $$u'=\omega_{0}x'+ix''=\omega_{0}x'-i\omega_{0}^{2}x-i\frac{\varepsilon\gamma}{m}x'=-i\omega_{0}u-i\frac{\varepsilon\gamma}{m}\operatorname{Im}u,$$ so differentiating $\zeta$ with the product and chain rules of [F2] gives $\zeta'=-\frac{i\varepsilon\gamma}{m}\frac{e^{i\omega_{0}t}}{\sqrt{2\omega_{0}}}\operatorname{Im}u=\varepsilon F(t,\zeta)$. Conversely, if $\zeta$ solves $\zeta'=\varepsilon F(t,\zeta)$ and $u:=\sqrt{2\omega_{0}}e^{-i\omega_{0}t}\zeta$, then $u'=-i\omega_{0}u-i(\varepsilon\gamma/m)\operatorname{Im}u$, so $x:=\operatorname{Re}(u)/\omega_{0}$ satisfies $x'=\operatorname{Re}(u')/\omega_{0}=\operatorname{Im}u$ and $x''=\operatorname{Im}(u')=-\omega_{0}\operatorname{Re}u-(\varepsilon\gamma/m)\operatorname{Im}u=-\omega_{0}^{2}x-(\varepsilon\gamma/m)x'$, that is, $x$ is a motion with the stated inverse formula. The two constructions are inverse to each other because $x$ and $x'$ are recovered from $\zeta$ and $\zeta$ is recovered from $x,x'$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

Smoothness, periodicity and average. $F$ is smooth on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb C$ because $\zeta\mapsto F(t,\zeta)$ is real-linear and the coefficients $t\mapsto e^{i\omega_{0}t}\cos(\omega_{0}t)$ and $t\mapsto e^{i\omega_{0}t}\sin(\omega_{0}t)$ are smooth; it is $P$-periodic with $P=2\pi/\omega_{0}$ because $e^{i\omega_{0}(t+P)}=e^{i\omega_{0}t}$ and $\cos(\omega_{0}(t+P))=\cos(\omega_{0}t)$, $\sin(\omega_{0}(t+P))=\sin(\omega_{0}t)$. Expanding the product, $$F(t,\zeta)=\frac{\gamma}{m}\Bigl(\sin(\omega_{0}t)\cos(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Im}\zeta-\sin^{2}(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Re}\zeta\Bigr)-\frac{i\gamma}{m}\Bigl(\cos^{2}(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Im}\zeta-\sin(\omega_{0}t)\cos(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Re}\zeta\Bigr),$$ so by [F3] the one-period average of the first bracket is $-\gamma\operatorname{Re}\zeta/(2m)$ and that of the second is $-\gamma\operatorname{Im}\zeta/(2m)$, giving $\bar F(\zeta)=-\frac{\gamma}{2m}(\operatorname{Re}\zeta+i\operatorname{Im}\zeta)=-\frac{\gamma}{2m}\zeta$.
